All three maps verified visually. The game is complete and the server is running right now.

## Smash Arena is ready to play 🎮

**Play now:** the server is already live — open **http://localhost:3000** in your browser. To start it again later: `cd C:\Users\aranr\claude-projects\ideal\smash-arena` then `npm start`.

**Playing with friends:**
- Same wifi — the server console prints a `Network: http://...` URL they can open directly.
- Over the internet — run `npx localtunnel --port 3000` and share the URL it prints (ngrok/cloudflared work too).

**The flow you asked for, exactly:** join screen → waiting room (host starts when everyone's in) → character select (pick + ready) → map vote (majority wins) → 3-2-1-GO battle with 3 lives each → fall off the stage and you lose a stock → last one standing wins → victory screen → cycles back to character select.

**Fighters** (all art and animation generated procedurally — skeletal keyframed poses, no asset files):
- **BLAZE** — flaming roundhouse-kick smash
- **TITAN** — slow heavyweight, double-hammer slam, hard to launch
- **VOLT** — fastest, triple jump, rising uppercut with lightning sparks
- **SHADE** — katana with the longest reach, sweeping slash trails

**Maps:** Sky Sanctuary (floating platforms), Neon Grid (flat synthwave stage), Ember Peaks (three islands over lava with rising embers).

**Combat is Smash-style:** damage % grows knockback, double jumps, fast-fall, drop-through platforms, hitstun, respawn invincibility, dynamic zooming camera, screen shake, hit sparks, KO explosions, and synthesized music/SFX (M to mute).

**Controls:** A/D or arrows to move, W/↑/Space to jump, S/↓ to fast-fall/drop, J/Z quick attack, K/X smash attack.

**Verified working:** an automated smoke test ran two bot clients through the entire cycle (lobby → select → vote → battle → KOs → victory → back to select) and passed; every character × animation × map render was exercised without errors, and the screenshots above are from the real game. There's also `public/test-scene.html?map=...` if you ever want a static render of any stage, and `node smoke-test.js` to re-verify the full loop.

One honest note: this uses simple snapshot interpolation (~100 ms buffer), which feels smooth on LAN and fine for casual internet play, but a tunnel adds latency — if it ever feels floaty with far-away friends, hosting on a small VPS closer to everyone is the fix.
